column1: # How well each table's digits are known.
# One line per table: tid, level, and the evidence for it. Read by
# `manage.py set_rigour`, which writes the level into the table's Data
# properties. Kept as a file rather than done in a script so that the
# judgement can be read, argued with and corrected -- it is a claim about
# 88 tables and most of it was made by reading one line of each generator.
# The evidence is the generate.sage that produced the table, in the
# numberdb-data repository. Tables with no script are deliberately absent: an
# absent level means nobody has established one, which is the truth for them.
# The four physical constants are `measured`, which is not on the scale the
# other levels sit on. It says the number was not computed at all, so asking
# whether measurement beats agreement-checking has no answer -- they are not
# A first pass classified these by pattern-matching the scripts and got
# thirteen wrong, in three separate ways: `mpmath.mp.airyaizero(` does not
# match `mpmath\.\w+\(`; `from mpmath import mp` hides mpmath behind `mp`;
# and six p-adic scripts import mpmath, never call it, and compute in Qp,
# which tracks precision exactly as an interval field does. Every line that
# is not `exact` by the table's declared type has since been read.
# The direction that matters was checked separately: a wrong `heuristic` is
# conservative, a wrong `proven` is a false claim of rigour. Every `proven`
# was re-checked against a deliberately wide net for inexact arithmetic, and
# the one hit turned out to be a `.n()` inside a debugging print.
# That check was not enough. Reading a script cannot tell you whether
# `RIF(f(x))` is an enclosure: it depends on whether f has an interval
# implementation, and when it does not, Sage evaluates numerically and hands
# back an interval of width zero -- which looks exactly like an exact value.
# Running each function settled it. gamma, psi, zeta and log return genuine
# enclosures; elliptic_kc, elliptic_ec, elliptic_pi and sin_integral return
# points that do not contain a 4000-bit value. Four tables were labelled
# `proven` on that basis and are now `heuristic`. Their stored digits are
# right -- they agree with a 4000-bit computation past 200 characters -- but
# nothing proves them, which is the distinction this file exists to draw.
# A table with a generator in `generators/` is described by that generator,
# not by this file: the generator is what runs, and it may do better than the
# script it replaced. Nine lines below say `converted:` for that reason, and
# running this file with --overwrite before they did cost those nine tables
# their levels for about a minute.
